skill.name: buying-committee-mapper
skill.description: Compare the contacts on an open deal with the roles expected to influence or approve it. Use Leadsets to find candidates at the same company and review them before adding approved contacts to your CRM.
skill.summary: Map stakeholder gaps on an open deal and review candidates for your CRM.
skill.author: leadsets

security_audit.summary: The Leadsets endpoint supports account searches and contact enrichment, so external data handling is a real part of the workflow. The other 20 alerts are documentation matches, with no evidence of shell execution, environment access, or system reconnaissance. The workflow leaves room for inconsistent email verification, CRM updates, and export approval.

remediation.issue: External processing of account and candidate data
remediation.suggestion: Disclose which inputs go to Leadsets and confirm the service is approved for the account. Send only required search filters and candidate identifiers.
Remove blanket claims that enrichment verifies email addresses. Require an explicit verified status before labeling or saving a primary email, and omit unverified addresses from CRM notes by default.

remediation.issue: Unclear scope of approved CRM writes
remediation.suggestion: Show the exact records, field changes, and associations for approval. Permit only the approved changes, and resolve duplicates without overwriting existing values.
Keep the review table in the conversation by default. Export only on explicit request and confirm the destination and sharing permissions before creating a Google Sheet.

content.user_title: Map the Buying Committee for an Open Deal
content.value_statement: An open deal can lack contacts for key decisions, even when you have an internal champion. Compare your contacts with expected roles and review candidates from the same company before adding them.
actual_capabilities: Maps existing deal contacts to expected committee roles and lists uncovered roles.
Checks Leadsets usage and tests the company domain with a one-result search.
Searches the account by role, function, and seniority, then ranks candidates and filters out known contacts.
Enriches shortlisted candidates to check their current employer and report available work email statuses.
Produces a review table with match reasons, uncovered roles, and candidates who changed employers.
Supports CSV or Google Sheets export and can add approved contacts through a connected CRM.
limitations: Search and enrichment require a Leadsets account and an MCP connection or REST API access. Usage limits apply.
CRM access requires a separate connection. You can provide the domain and existing contacts without one.
Job titles suggest likely committee roles but do not prove decision authority. Work emails may be missing or unconfirmed.
Searches stay within the account domain. The skill does not provide phone numbers or send outreach.

use_cases.title: Find missing approvers before a deal review
use_cases.description: Compare attached contacts with expected approvers and review account matches for uncovered roles.

use_cases.title: Plan outreach beyond one contact
use_cases.description: Use a company domain and a short contact list to identify a likely economic buyer and technical evaluator.

use_cases.title: Review contacts before adding them to the CRM
use_cases.description: Check suggested contacts against the account and deal, confirm their current employer, and review the records before approval.

prompt_templates.title: List missing committee roles
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the contacts for [deal name] with the default buying committee roles. Show which roles are covered and which are missing. Stop before searching for people.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start with a CRM deal and check role coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Find finance and technical candidates
prompt_templates.prompt: At [company domain], find a likely finance approver and technical evaluator. Exclude these existing contacts: [names and titles]. Return up to three candidates with match reasons. Do not write to the CRM.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use a domain and a contact list without relying on a CRM lookup.

prompt_templates.title: Limit search and enrichment usage
prompt_templates.prompt: For [deal name], check Leadsets usage and test the account domain with one result. Search only for [roles] and return up to 10 results per role. Enrich no more than four people. Report unmatched roles and use the returned email statuses.
prompt_templates.scenario: Review a shortlist within defined search and enrichment limits.

prompt_templates.title: Review proposed CRM additions
prompt_templates.prompt: Map [deal name] and show proposed additions for [CRM], including roles, match reasons, email statuses, and account and deal associations. Skip existing contacts. Wait for my approval before writing. Use a primary email only when its status is verified.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a controlled update to a connected CRM.

best_practices: Confirm the company domain and expected committee roles before searching.
Check remaining Leadsets usage and set a shortlist size before enrichment.
Review identities, returned email statuses, and exact CRM changes before approving any write.
anti_patterns: Treating a job title as proof that a person can approve the purchase.
Treating catch-all or unknown addresses as verified work emails.
Approving a CRM write or shared export without checking the records and destination.

faq.question: What do I need to get started?
faq.answer: Provide an open deal name or company domain. You also need a Leadsets account and a connected MCP server or REST API access.

faq.question: Can I use it without a CRM connection?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the company domain and, when available, the names and titles of existing contacts. You can review the results without writing to a CRM.

faq.question: Which committee roles does it check by default?
faq.answer: It checks for an economic buyer, the champion's manager, a technical evaluator, an end-user lead, and a procurement or finance approver.

faq.question: Are work emails always verified?
faq.answer: No. Use the returned status and treat catch-all and unknown addresses as unconfirmed. A contact can also have no email.

faq.question: When does it add contacts to my CRM?
faq.answer: The workflow shows a review table before requesting approval. CRM writes require a connected CRM and your approval.

faq.question: Does it use Leadsets records?
faq.answer: Yes. Searches and enrichment use records when they return a person. Checking usage does not use records.
